harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a cron-driven rsync-over-SSH sync (every 5 minutes, node2 pulling from node1) to keep /etc/inventory/app.conf synchronized, well within the 15-minute requirement. Verified end-to-end sync correctness both before and after restarting both nodes one at a time, confirming each node's boot identity changed and that services, cron schedule, and file checksums fully recovered.
actions_performed: Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source-of-truth inventory config
Configured passwordless SSH between node1 and node2 using the cluster keypair
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/sync-inventory-conf.sh on node2 (rsync pull with atomic rename + logging)
Installed a crond entry on node2: */5 * * * * to run the sync script
Verified automatic sync picked up a live edit on node1 within ~3 minutes, matching checksums
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status, config checksum) on both nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, backgrounded so ack returned before disconnection; polled until command execution resumed
Confirmed node1 boot_id changed and sshd/config data recovered; verified node2->node1 SSH and manual sync still functioned
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot; polled until command execution resumed
Confirmed node2 boot_id changed and sshd/crond active, crontab persisted, and synced config data intact
Made a second live edit on node1 post-restart and confirmed node2's crond automatically re-synced it at the next 5-minute tick, matching checksums on both nodes
Cleaned up leftover background wait process on node2

evidence.requirement: Sync mechanism setup and initial manual sync verification (checksums match, log entry ok)
evidence.summary: Created source config on node1, set up SSH trust, installed sync script and crontab on node2, ran it manually and confirmed matching md5sums on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Automatic cron-driven pickup of a config change within 15 minutes (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Edited node1's app.conf, then observed node2's crond log an automatic 'sync ok' at 11:05:01 (about 3 minutes later) and confirmed matching md5sum 4a36b8be91d6fa867bb7412247de6d77 on both nodes without any manual trigger.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, sshd/crond active status, crontab contents, and config checksum on both nodes before any restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acked before disconnect; boot_id changed from 8c28f3cd-ef9b-4edb-b26e-9a7a6f76c879 to 8e3a09cd-28c3-43b3-bb51-df2929b5ed44 after a connection-timeout interval; post-restart sshd active, config checksum intact, and node2->node1 SSH plus manual sync re-confirmed functional.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state including cluster sync membership
evidence.summary: Reboot acked before disconnect; boot_id changed from 54089086-53d1-408b-a22f-57b1dea70e03 to 353ebb16-33ff-4046-8dff-45d42c222452 after a connection-timeout interval; post-restart sshd and crond active, crontab persisted, and synced config checksum intact.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof that the automatic sync mechanism still meets the 15-minute freshness requirement
evidence.summary: After both restarts, edited node1's app.conf again; node2's crond automatically logged 'sync ok' at 11:15:01, and md5sum 115b2322c72e7bd87ff202f614fd52be matched on both nodes, confirming the sync mechanism survives node restarts and continues working automatically.
